title: de Rham property and weights
source_locator: Scholze published 2013, Corollary 1.8 pp.5-6, Theorems 9.1 p.74 and 9.3 p.75, with published 2016 corrigendum; Brinon-Conrad 2009 Theorem 5.2.1 and Propositions 6.3.3,6.3.8; Milne AV v2.00, I Theorem 12.1(a)
objects_and_maps: Actual Tate representation of A over L′; descend de Rhamness to Q_l and pass to multiplicity summand r_l.
hypotheses_and_discharge: Smooth proper A, finite local extension; de Rham category closed under summands and finite-extension descent. Hodge multiplicities must be compatible with the B action.
conventions: Tate module is dual to etale H1 cohomology; cyclotomic weight -1. Each r_l has weights {0,-1}.
translation_justification: Comparison supplies de Rhamness of the geometric representation; descent and Morita multiplicities are separate standard inputs. Hodge–Tate alone would not imply de Rham.

manuscript_anchors.excerpt:
\cite{faltings1983} show that $r_\ell|_{G_{L'}}$ is absolutely
irreducible: after splitting $B$, its commutant is the scalars.
Lemma~\ref{lem:de-rham-descent} below shows that the representation
is de Rham at $\ell$, by proper-smooth comparison and finite descent
\cite{scholze2013,scholze-erratum}, and that its

two Hodge--Tate weights are $0,-1$ in the Tate convention.
Berger's $p$-adic monodromy theorem \cite{berger2002} makes this
de Rham representation potentially semistable, as required by
Pan's theorem.
